The submission supplies the required checker_correspondence item, the applicability item and a resolution for the inherited input issue aa5f0ccb4bf14c69994ca8160b854bea, which still applies to this artifact because the earlier resolution covered only the first scenario's lineage. The correspondence item (no_issue_found, 9 cited ranges, 5 retained limitations) states that this artifact is a second scenario of the same accepted requirement rather than a new proposition, because the claim's scope already covers the window in which a client call is raced with Shutdown, and reviews the fixed inputs, legality, oracle, correlation and counterevidence together: a single-voter node built by the package's own NewRaft with the documented BatchApplyCh option so applyCh is buffered; a LogStore that holds exactly one StoreLogs call after arming (a latency injection on an injected dependency) that parks the main goroutine inside the leader's dispatch path; 200 requests issued from goroutines so the buffer fills and the rest block inside the enqueue select; and the public Shutdown, whose future joins the goroutine group. The oracle counts the accepted futures whose own completion channels are still empty after that join, with requests rejected as ErrRaftShutdown counted separately as completed, so a nonzero value means the node accepted work it never answered; the admission event precedes the result in the single runner stream with matching identity. The retained observation is the violation: requests_issued_while_active with node_state Leader and main_thread_busy true, then accepted_requests_observed with accepted 64, rejected_shutdown 136, completed_other 0, unresolved_total 64, node_state_after_shutdown Shutdown and the parked write finishing with leadership lost, at exit 0. Counterevidence is explicit: the parked dispatch path is what makes the buffer fill deterministically; the counts depend on the buffer size and on how many requests the loop picks up before it takes the shutdown case, which is why only the zero-unresolved assertion is made; the default unbuffered channel cannot accept a request that shutdown abandons, as the first scenario showed; only the Apply path with BatchApplyCh is exercised; and no caller-side timeout is measured. The applicability item (no_issue_found, 9 cited ranges, 3 limitations) argues why the implementation owes completion for work it accepted while leading — Apply's contract makes the returned future the completion channel, and the implementation itself answers accepted work when it can, failing inflight work with ErrLeadershipLost and unenqueueable work with ErrRaftShutdown, while the buffering, the enqueue select, the shutdown join and the futures' missing escape are all the library's own — and retains the inherited condition as an outstanding-repair boundary rather than a discharge. The resolution answers that condition with the same reasoning applied to this artifact and cites both executions of the unit, declaring no residual issues and keeping the repair location and the schedule dependence as scope limitations. With the inherited blocker and the correspondence blocker answered, the assessment for this artifact should recompute to a confirmed violated comparison, which completes the unit's second scenario and leaves the run at six confirmed findings with the frontier limited to whether the dual leadership can be made to persist, whether production TCP scheduling reproduces the heartbeat interleaving, and the deferred surface about the commit context a follower leaves after installing a snapshot.
